aria: Animated recap of the Celtics' 98 to 93 road win at Toronto: Jayson Tatum's go-ahead free throw with 25.2 seconds left that made it 94 to 93, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 24 points and 8 assists, the top scorers, how the Celtics won, and the next game at home against Dallas.
notes: Box score from the Celtics' 98–93 road win over the Toronto Raptors on Nov 11, 2026, from the Covers.com box score and the Land of Basketball box score, with game details from CBS Boston (AP), Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker) and the CBS Sports play-by-play. All 98 Celtics points and all 93 Raptors points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (Toronto 61–54 at the half, 80–75 after three). Biggest leads: Boston's 5 and Toronto's 22 (Covers.com); Toronto led 59–37 after a Jamal Shead free throw with 5:24 left in the second quarter, and Boston answered with 16 straight points, the first 10 by Tatum (CBS Boston). Records and conference ranks are from the site's standings (data/season.json) after Wednesday's games: Boston 10–2 (first in the east), Dallas 7–4.

Paul George sat out with an illness, the night after scoring 36 in Philadelphia, and it was the second night of a back-to-back (CBS Boston; the site's schedule). It was Boston's fifth straight win; Toronto fell to 5–6, below .500 for the first time this season (CBS Boston). Toronto made 10 of 18 threes in the first quarter and 6 of 25 the rest of the way (CBS Boston). Boston hosts Dallas on Sunday, Nov 15 at 6:00 PM ET (Ball Exclusives; CBS Boston).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jayson Tatum's free throws with 25.2 seconds left: the first tied it 93–93 and the second put Boston ahead 94–93 for good (CBS Boston; Ball Exclusives; CBS Sports play-by-play, which has Toronto ahead 93–92 before the trip to the line). Queta and Hauser then made four free throws for the final margin (CBS Sports play-by-play). The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Boston Celtics or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Tatum’s listed 6-foot-8 and 210 pounds (RealGM), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-11 wingspan measured at the 2016 Nike Hoop Summit (DraftExpress), in the Celtics' road kit with his look from the site's looks file. His No. 0 is from RealGM. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
